analysis: The code calls descriptor.getFields().get(i) inside a loop from i=0 to i<cellsToProcess. Before the loop, there is a check: if cells.size() > descriptor.getFields().size(), then either an exception is thrown (if ignoreUnkownValues is false) or cellsToProcess is set to descriptor.getFields().size() (if ignoreUnkownValues is true). If cells.size() <= descriptor.getFields().size(), cellsToProcess = cells.size(). In all cases, i is within [0, descriptor.getFields().size()-1] because cellsToProcess <= descriptor.getFields().size(). Additionally, i is never negative. Therefore, the index is always valid, and the IndexOutOfBoundsException is avoided.
answer: The declared exception IndexOutOfBoundsException is avoided by the bounds checks on cellsToProcess and the loop condition.
remark: The IndexOutOfBoundsException could only be thrown if i is less than 0 or greater than or equal to the size of the list (descriptor.getFields().size()). However, the code ensures i is always between 0 and cellsToProcess-1, and cellsToProcess is set to at most descriptor.getFields().size(). Thus, the exception is never triggered in this context.
